payload.theorem_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Normalize the original summand so that the only remaining denominators are (-q^d;q^d)_k, and clear all of them by the common factor D_{d,n}(q). Introduce the auxiliary parameter a and prove two independent divisibilities for the cleared difference F(a,q): first, divisibility by (a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}) via the special value a=q^{-rn}, the exact terminating evaluation there, and the symmetry a↦a^{-1}; second, divisibility by [n]_q via the separate root-of-unity/[n]_q analysis. Combine the two divisibilities because the factors are coprime, then specialize a=1 to obtain divisibility by [n]_q(1-q^{rn})^2. Finally, use (1-q^{rn})^2 ⊇ Φ_n(q)^2 and the coprimality of D_{d,n}(q) with [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 to cancel D_{d,n}(q) and recover the original theorem.

steps.derives: From the theorem hypotheses n > 1 and n ≡ 1 mod 2d, define m = (n-1)/(2d). Then m is a nonnegative integer, n is odd, gcd(d,n)=1, and rn = r + 2drm.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the arithmetic unpacking of the congruence condition n ≡ 1 mod 2d. The identities n=2dm+1 and rn=r+2drm are immediate after defining m, while n odd and gcd(d,n)=1 follow from n=1+2dm.

steps.derives: Let R(q) = [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}, let D(q) = ∏_{k=0}^{n-1} (-q^d;q^d)_k, let S(a,q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (a q^r, q^r/a, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k, let F(a,q) = D(q) (S(a,q) - R(q)), and let Δ(q) denote the theorem difference Δ(q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}. By Lemma L1, S(1,q) is exactly the finite sum appearing in Δ(q), so F(1,q) = D(q) · Δ(q).
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L1 rewrites the factor ((q^d;q^d)_k)^2/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k as (q^d;q^d)_k/(-q^d;q^d)_k term by term. Substituting a=1 into S(a,q) therefore reproduces the original theorem sum exactly, and the definition of F gives F(1,q)=D(q)(S(1,q)-R(q))=D(q)Δ(q).

steps.derives: The specialization S(q^{-rn},q) is equal to the terminating sum Σ_{k=0}^{rm} [3dk+r]_q (q^{-2drm}, q^{r+rn}, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the specialization and truncation statement of Lemma L3, using the m fixed in A0.
By A2, S(q^{-rn},q) is the terminating rm-sum displayed there. Lemma L5 evaluates precisely that terminating sum and gives the value R(q).
By definition F(a,q)=D(q)(S(a,q)-R(q)). Step A3 shows S(q^{-rn},q)=R(q), so the bracket vanishes and hence F(q^{-rn},q)=0.
This is exactly the symmetry statement of Lemma L4.

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial F(a,q) is divisible by (a - q^{rn})(1 - a q^{rn}).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L6 with H(a,q)=F(a,q) and N=rn. Step A5 supplies the symmetry H(a,q)=H(a^{-1},q), and Step A4 supplies the root H(q^{-rn},q)=0. Lemma L6 then yields divisibility by the full quadratic factor (a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}).

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial F(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of Lemma L7.

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial F(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q (a - q^{rn})(1 - a q^{rn}).
steps.trivial_justification: Step A7 gives divisibility by [n]_q, and Step A6 gives divisibility by the quadratic parameter factor. Lemma L8 states that these two factors are coprime in Z[q^{±1},a^{±1}], so simultaneous divisibility implies divisibility by their product.

steps.derives: After substituting a=1, the polynomial F(1,q) is divisible by [n]_q (1 - q^{rn})^2.
steps.trivial_justification: Evaluation at a=1 is a ring homomorphism from Z[q^{±1},a^{±1}] to Z[q^{±1}]. Applying it to the divisibility statement from A8 sends the factor (a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}) to (1-q^{rn})^2, so the specialized divisibility follows.

steps.derives: The specialized value F(1,q) is divisible by [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L9 shows that [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 divides [n]_q (1-q^{rn})^2. Step A9 shows the latter divides F(1,q). Therefore [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 divides F(1,q).

By A0, the hypotheses needed for Lemma L2 hold, so D(q)=∏_{k=0}^{n-1}(-q^d;q^d)_k is coprime to [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Step A1 gives F(1,q)=D(q)Δ(q), where Δ(q) is exactly the theorem difference. Step A10 shows [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 divides F(1,q). Coprime cancellation of D(q) therefore implies that [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 divides Δ(q), which is exactly the stated congruence.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let (x;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 - x q^j). For every positive integer d and every integer k ≥ 0, one has ((q^d;q^d)_k)^2 / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k = (q^d;q^d)_k / (-q^d;q^d)_k. Consequently, replacing the factor ((q^d;q^d)_k)^2 / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k in the theorem summand by (q^d;q^d)_k / (-q^d;q^d)_k leaves the summand unchanged.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: Pure algebraic normalization of q-factorials; no congruence or cyclotomic argument is involved.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (x;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 - x q^j), and let (x,y,z;q)_k = (x;q)_k (y;q)_k (z;q)_k. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and let n > 1 satisfy n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Write m = (n-1)/(2d), and define S_{d,r,n}(a,q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (a q^r, q^r/a, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k. Then S_{d,r,n}(q^{-rn},q) = Σ_{k=0}^{rm} [3dk+r]_q (q^{-2drm}, q^{r+rn}, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k. Equivalently, every term with k > rm vanishes after the specialization a = q^{-rn} because (q^{-2drm}; q^{2d})_k = 0 for k > rm.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It only analyzes the effect of one special parameter value and proves termination, without any cyclotomic divisibility.

For positive integers d, r, n, define S_{d,r,n}(a,q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (a q^r, q^r/a, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k, define D_{d,n}(q) = ∏_{k=0}^{n-1} (-q^d;q^d)_k, define R_{d,r,n}(q) = [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}, and define F_{d,r,n}(a,q) = D_{d,n}(q) ( S_{d,r,n}(a,q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) ). Then F_{d,r,n}(a,q) = F_{d,r,n}(a^{-1},q) in the Laurent polynomial ring Z[q^{±1},a^{±1}].

Define D_{d,n}(q) = ∏_{k=0}^{n-1} (-q^d;q^d)_k, define S_{d,r,n}(a,q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (a q^r, q^r/a, q^d; q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (-q^d;q^d)_k, and define F_{d,r,n}(a,q) = D_{d,n}(q) ( S_{d,r,n}(a,q) - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2} ). lemmas.statement_nl: Let [n]_q = (1-q^n)/(1-q). In the Laurent polynomial ring Z[q^{±1},a^{±1}], for every positive integers n and N the two elements [n]_q and (a - q^N)(1 - a q^N) are coprime. Consequently, if H(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q and also divisible by (a - q^N)(1 - a q^N), then H(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q (a - q^N)(1 - a q^N).
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This is a general coprime-product lemma in a Laurent polynomial ring; it does not use the special form of the q-series.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q) and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. For all positive integers r and n, one has 1 - q^{rn} = (1 - q^n) Σ_{j=0}^{r-1} q^{jn}. candidates.strategy_summary: Introduce an auxiliary parameter a by replacing the duplicated factor (q^r,q^r;q^{2d})_k with (a q^r,q^r/a;q^{2d})_k, normalize the original denominator via ((q^d;q^d)_k)^2/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k/(-q^d;q^d)_k, clear the remaining odd denominators by a common factor D_{d,n}(q), prove the parameter-factor divisibility from the special value a=q^{-rn} plus the symmetry a↦a^{-1}, prove the independent [n]_q-divisibility after clearing denominators, then specialize a=1 and use (1-q^{rn})^2 to recover the Φ_n(q)^2 factor.
